evidence_trigger: Root Cause: A router memory hardware failure disrupted synchronization during routine automated maintenance.

evidence_trigger: Initial summary, root cause: Control-host failover activated an existing logic bug, generating excessive exchanges between the datacenter control system and equipment.
evidence_fault: Initial summary: Overheated EC2 hosts shut down in part of one zone; EBS volumes degraded, APIs returned errors, and excessive exchanges overwhelmed internal cooling controls.

evidence_trigger: November 3 incident section: A high volume of poorly optimized API calls triggered an inefficient database query.
evidence_fault: November 3 incident section: Backlogged webhook and background jobs delayed workflow starts and deliveries; several GitHub services returned more errors.

evidence_trigger: What went wrong, and why? A failed utility transmission wire tripped substation breakers, cutting utility power across West US 2.
evidence_fault: What went wrong, and why? Backup power failures took some servers offline in two datacenters; neither datacenter was lost entirely.

evidence_trigger: Primary Outage: A utility transformer failure cut power. EBS Software Bug Impacting Snapshots: A separate hardware failure left the snapshot reference list incomplete.
evidence_fault: Primary Outage: Power loss shut down most EC2 instances in the affected zone, severed network links, and caused API errors and queue overload.

evidence_trigger: Impact Summary: A routine GitHub Actions deployment temporarily reduced pod capacity at one site, shifting traffic to the remaining sites.
evidence_fault: What went wrong and why?: Overload caused CPU throttling, out-of-memory restarts, and cache, DNS, and API errors; retries of revoked jobs grew the backlog.
